name: Guideline-Clarity Insights
problem: Managers cannot currently see which guidelines repeatedly cause confusion, revisions or overrides. A single draft view hides recurring policy problems.
design: Snapshot policy revision/text on each finding. Store structured override categories alongside original reasons. Aggregate issue frequency, override rate, repeat edits and decision time by policy revision, channel and date, with denominators. Add a Manager/Admin insights endpoint and dashboard linking every alert to permission-checked source findings. Require minimum sample counts; suggested clarifications remain human proposals.
milestones: M1: add policy revision snapshots, override categories and fixture-based aggregation tests.
M2: deliver counts, rates, date filters and drill-down to real evidence.
M3: add ambiguity signals and optional grounded summaries; test small-sample and access-control cases.
success: Proposed acceptance measures: all displayed aggregates exactly match event fixtures; every alert links to its supporting findings; no alerts below the declared sample threshold. In a future human study, compare task completion time for identifying a recurring guideline problem against the draft-by-draft baseline. No improvement percentage is claimed before measurement.
cut: Cut AI clustering/summaries first, then advanced cohort filters. Keep policy revisions, counts with denominators, override reasons and evidence drill-down.
form_answer: Guideline-Clarity Insights will help managers see which brand rules repeatedly confuse creators. It will combine finding history and override reasons into a recurring-issue dashboard with counts, rates and links to the underlying drafts. Versioned guideline snapshots will keep old and new wording separate, and minimum sample counts will prevent weak signals from being presented as conclusions. Managers will use those examples to clarify guidelines while keeping every policy change under human approval. Success will be measured by reproducible aggregates and a future comparison of the time needed to identify recurring problems; AI summaries will be cut first if time is short.

name: Multi-format review of images and DOCX/PDF
problem: Creators currently must paste text; they cannot submit an image, brochure or document and inspect a finding at its original page or image region.
design: Add private Asset and ExtractedSpan records with file hash, MIME type, extraction coverage, page/paragraph coordinates and version. Validate file signatures and size/page limits; isolate parsing. Extract DOCX paragraphs/tables with python-docx and PDF text with pypdf/pdfplumber; use OCR for scanned pages. For images, check supplied alt text, measurable contrast, palette and logo presence with OCR/vision assistance. Evaluate the requested qwen/qwen3.8-27b only after confirming provider vision support, otherwise select a supported vision model behind an adapter. Reuse rules, grounding, decisions and approval; show cannot determine when evidence or extraction is inadequate.
milestones: M1: implement validated uploads and DOCX/selectable-PDF extraction with source locations and coverage warnings.
M2: add image/OCR ingestion, alt-text review and measured palette/contrast checks.
M3: add supported vision/logo checks and scanned-PDF OCR; integrate asset versions and source-region review.
success: Proposed acceptance measures: every retained finding maps to an original paragraph, page or image region; fixture tests detect corrupt/oversize files and unreadable pages without claiming complete extraction. Measure extraction coverage and per-check precision/recall on labelled format fixtures, then have a human complete review-to-approval on each supported format. Complex contrast must return cannot determine instead of an invented ratio.
cut: Cut custom logo detection and broad visual aesthetics first, then scanned-PDF OCR if needed. Keep DOCX/selectable-PDF extraction, basic image/alt-text checks, coverage warnings and source-located findings; do not advertise an unsupported format as complete.
form_answer: Multi-format review will let creators submit images and DOCX/PDF files instead of copying everything into a text box. Document extraction will preserve page or paragraph locations so a finding can be checked against the original source. Image review will cover alt text, measurable contrast, brand palette and logo checks, with vision support used only after the provider capability is verified. Unsupported or unreadable regions will be marked for a human rather than guessed, and the existing decisions, versions and approvals will remain in use. We will measure extraction coverage, source-location correctness and labelled check quality; advanced logo and aesthetic checks will be cut before the basic document workflow.

name: Reliability and evaluation harness
problem: The current 11-draft sample set is too small to establish general accuracy, and accepting a suggestion does not prove that it was correct. Users need clearer evidence of what a review system can reliably detect.
design: Build a versioned human-labelled benchmark with separate development/evaluation splits, uncertain cases and adjudication. Record expected code, span, severity and safety labels. Pin results to code commit, KB/prompt hash, provider/model and timestamp; separate cache replays from new calls. Add finding-level correctness/source/severity/safety feedback distinct from accept/reject. Report per-code/channel precision and recall, span quality, fabricated-citation and unsafe-replacement rates, latency, token cost and fallback behavior. Display benchmark date, counts and uncertainty next to metrics; confidence remains uncalibrated until evaluated.
milestones: M1: define labels, annotation guide, split and deterministic CI runner with failure injection.
M2: store reproducible model runs and finding-level feedback; adjudicate disagreements.
M3: publish benchmark-scoped metrics in the UI, add confidence-bin analysis and compare model/prompt revisions.
success: Proposed acceptance measures: 100% of displayed metrics reproduce from stored labels/results; all provider-failure fixtures complete via a documented fallback or rules-only result; no known fabricated citation or rule-violating replacement passes the safety fixtures. Set quality release thresholds only after a labelled baseline exists and show sample counts and uncertainty. Confidence calibration and independent human evaluation are future measurements, not current claims.
cut: Cut live model-comparison dashboards, automated calibration and continuous paid evaluations first. Keep a fixed labelled benchmark, reproducible offline runner, failure fixtures, feedback records and honest metric scope.
form_answer: The reliability and evaluation harness will make review quality measurable beyond our own 11 sample drafts. A versioned human-labelled benchmark will test citations, spans, unsupported claims, unsafe replacements, workflow routing and provider failures. Users will be able to report a wrong finding separately from deciding whether to change their draft. The UI will show benchmark-scoped precision and recall with counts and evaluation dates, while model confidence remains labelled as uncalibrated until measured. Success means reproducible metrics and repeatable failure handling; live comparison dashboards and automated calibration will be cut before the fixed benchmark and feedback workflow.
